name: neuroinfections overview
title: Suspected meningitis or encephalitis: blood culture and empiric treatment first, CT before the lumbar puncture only with focal signs or a decreased level of consciousness, then the CSF separates bacterial meningitis, aseptic (viral) meningitis and herpes simplex encephalitis, each with its organisms and treatment

root.title: Fever · headache · stiff neck · altered mental status: think MENINGITIS
lines: classic triad: FEVER, ALTERED MENTAL STATUS, NUCHAL RIGIDITY (Kernig's, Brudzinski's)
language trouble, confusion, focal seizures → think ENCEPHALITIS (the brain itself)
4 kinds of CNS infection: bacterial (meningitis, abscess) · viral (meningitis, encephalitis) · fungal (cryptococcal) · protozoal (neurocysticercosis)

groups.title: Suspected CNS infection: treat FIRST, then let the CSF decide

pres.title: Plan
lines: 2 · START EMPIRIC treatment now: never wait for the CT or the tap

3 · CT/MRI FIRST only if focal signs or ↓ consciousness (PUNISH: Papilledema, Unconscious, Neurologic deficit, Immunocompromised, Seizure, History of CNS disease) · also poorly seen fundi, from a NEUROCYSTICERCOSIS area → mass = NEUROSURGERY
4 · LUMBAR PUNCTURE (cell count, protein, glucose + a SERUM glucose, Gram stain, culture) → adjust treatment to the CSF

head: h
Bacterial meningitis
any age · a clinical EMERGENCY
clue: case: 34 y teacher, 2 days · T 38.9, oriented, moderate neck stiffness · CT normal
csf: • protein HIGH (500-10,000) · glucose LOW (under 2.5; CSF:serum < 0.3-0.4, normal > 0.6)
case: cloudy, 10,500 polys, Gram + diplococci, glucose 1.5, protein 2500 → NEISSERIA
• adults: S. pneumoniae (Gram + lance diplococci), N. meningitidis (Gram − kidney diplococci, vaccine), H. influenzae (fewer since vaccine)
• neonates: E. coli, group B strep
tx: • CEFTRIAXONE 2 g q12h: H. flu, meningococcus, sensitive pneumococcus, MSSA
• + VANCOMYCIN 1 g q8h: resistant pneumococcus, MRSA
• + AMPICILLIN 2 g q4h if > 50 or immunocompromised: Listeria
with the FIRST antibiotic dose, then q6h for 4 days
~ ↓ morbidity + mortality, most in S. pneumoniae

head: h
Aseptic (viral) meningitis
no organism isolated
clue: case: 20 y student, aches, T 37.8, irritable, mild neck stiffness

head: h
Herpes simplex encephalitis
the BRAIN itself · MESIAL TEMPORAL lobes
clue: • focal seizures, impaired memory, focal deficits
• fever, ↓ awareness · usually NO stiff neck · OLDER patients
case: 47 y, 3 days fever, turned the wrong way on the 401 · T 38.1, nonsensical, not following commands
csf: case: 230 lymphocytes, 56 red cells, glucose 4.0, protein 2000 · MRI + EEG both temporal lobes
tx: meningoencephalitis (stiff neck + weakness + seizures) → antibiotics + acyclovir, then CT/MRI

panels.title: CSF: normal values
items: CSF:serum glucose over 0.6 · Gram stain empty
